glosses: Situation particulièrement fastidieuse ou lassante.

examples.text: Je t’écris ceci sur mon carton dans la classe de ce bon père Gors qui disserte sur le plus grand commun diviseur d’un emmerdement sans égal, qui m'étourdit si bien que je n’y entends goutte, n’y vois que du feu.

Simplement parce que l’homme le plus maladivement rangeur au monde, sinon le plus rangé, je me représente sans arrêt l’extrême emmerdement d’avoir sans arrêt à rouvrir et refermer toutes ces boîtes remplies de tous ces disques à désempocheter et à rempocheter sans arrêt.

examples.text: Das leichte Zittern seiner rechten Hand, das bisher nur ein Ärgernis war, würde sich verstärken.

glosses: A psychedelic crisis; hallucinogenic drug use producing undesirable dysphoric psychological effects, most often fear, paranoia, and especially horrifying hallucinations; a bad trip.

examples.text: This young man never had a bummer in some 33 LSD trips. Every one of the them was a delight—everything under control. He needed only to snap his fingers, and down he came, anytime. But on Voyage 34, he finally met himself coming down an up staircase, and the encounter was crushing.

glosses: Exclamation of annoyance or frustration at a bummer (disappointment).

examples.text: You know, the kind of guy who would, if he wasn't gay, probably be shouting ‘Oi, gay boy!’ or ‘You bummer!’ or even ‘Oi, paki!’ or what have you. They're not enlightened.

glosses: News of unpleasant, unfortunate or sad events.

examples.text: One of the rules of journalism is that news from Africa is always bad news.

"Oh, help!" said Pooh. "I'd better go back."
"Oh, bother!" said Pooh. "I shall have to go on."

glosses: To be troubled; to give way to mental anxiety or doubt.

examples.text: So you go along for a long time / And nothing seems to worry your mind / But what it adds up to / It's the side effect / That finally gets to you

glosses: Disturb the peace of mind of; afflict with mental agitation or distress; to exercise.

examples.text: Your tone of voice worries me.

glosses: To harass; to irritate or distress.

examples.text: The President was worried into military action by persistent advisors.

glosses: To seize or shake by the throat, especially of a dog or wolf.

glosses: To touch repeatedly; to fiddle with.

examples.text: Christian paced the caravan, worrying his beard.

glosses: To strangle.

examples.text: We read (Law's Memor. Pref. lix.) that "one John Brugh, a notorious warlock (wizard) in the parochin of Fossoquhy, by the space of thirty-six years, was worried at a stake and burned, 1643."

examples.text: My main worry is that I'll miss the train.

glosses: A person who causes worry.

examples.text: They could never make him speak a word, although he was old enough, in short, he was a perfect worry night and day.
